candidates.comment: A LinkRole is an intangible role representing a Web link, allowing for the specification of link relationships and other HTML link element details outside of HTML. Also called URL role, hyperlink descriptor, web link attribute. Examples: a link with 'linkRelationship' 'amphtml', a canonical URL link, a link to a related resource.

candidates.label: ControlAction
candidates.comment: An action where an agent operates or manages a device or application. Also called controlling, operating, managing, manipulating. Examples: Turning on a light, adjusting a thermostat, launching a software application, steering a car. Distinct from Action, which is a general activity.

types.embedding_query_text: StrategyCategory: A classification or type of strategy. Also called strategy type, strategic domain, planning category. Examples: defensive strategies for AI.

chosen_type.label: StrategyCategory
chosen_type.definition: A classification or type of strategy.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents a 'StrategyCategory'. It is an intangible classification.

candidates.label: MapCategoryType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of different categories or kinds of maps. Also called map type, map classification, cartography category. Examples: "RoadMap", "SatelliteMap", "TerrainMap", "HybridMap".

candidates.label: PhysicalActivityCategory
candidates.comment: PhysicalActivityCategory is an enumeration for categories of physical activity, organized by physiologic classification. Also called exercise type, activity classification. Examples: AerobicActivity, StrengthTraining, Flexibility. Distinct from PhysicalActivity, which is an instance of an activity.

candidates.label: CategoryCodeSet
candidates.comment: A creative work that defines a collection of related category codes. Also called classification system, code list, taxonomy. Examples: The UNSPSC classification, a company's internal product category list, a set of industry codes.

candidates.label: CategoryCode
candidates.comment: A defined term representing a specific code within a classification system. Also called classification code, item code, type code. Examples: UNSPSC code for office supplies, NAICS code for manufacturing, a product category ID.

candidates.label: TierBenefitEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of specific benefits offered as part of a loyalty or membership program. Also called loyalty program benefit, membership perk, reward tier. Examples: free shipping, early access to sales, exclusive content, dedicated customer support.

types.embedding_query_text: RegulatoryMechanism: A system or method used to control or govern an activity or process. Also called control mechanism, governance tool, oversight system. Examples: legal frameworks, policies.

chosen_type.label: Legislation
chosen_type.justification: A 'RegulatoryMechanism' like 'legal frameworks' and 'policies' are forms of or closely related to 'Legislation', which represents legal documents and rules.

candidates.label: WatchAction
candidates.comment: The act of consuming dynamic or moving visual content. Also called view, observe, see. Examples: watching a movie, watching a live sports broadcast, watching a video tutorial.

candidates.label: Legislation
candidates.comment: Legislation is a creative work representing a legal document such as an act, decree, or bill, or a component thereof. Also called law, statute, legal act, regulation. Examples: the Civil Rights Act, a local ordinance, a proposed bill in parliament. Distinct from LegislationObject, which is a specific file containing the legislation.

candidates.label: SuspendAction
candidates.comment: The act of momentarily pausing a device, application, or process. Also called pausing, halting, putting on hold, temporarily stopping. Examples: pausing music playback, suspending a computer process, pausing a timer.

candidates.label: TradeAction
candidates.comment: The act of exchanging goods or services for monetary compensation. Also called commerce, transaction, selling. Examples: a business selling products to customers, a consultant providing services for a fee, an artist selling their artwork.

types.embedding_query_text: Capability: The ability or power to do something. Also called capacity, ability, competence. Examples: technical capabilities.

chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents a 'Capability'. It is an intangible quality or attribute.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: Service
candidates.comment: An intangible offering provided by an organization, such as delivery, consulting, or repair. Also called offering, provision, assistance, support. Examples: a car repair service, a legal consulting service, a package delivery service, a web hosting service.

candidates.label: Permit
candidates.comment: A Permit is an intangible entity representing an official authorization issued by an organization. Also called license, authorization, pass. Examples: a building permit, a parking permit, a fishing license. Distinct from LegalService, which is a service, not the document itself.

candidates.label: TechArticle
candidates.comment: An article providing technical information, such as how-to guides, troubleshooting steps, or specifications. Also called technical guide, how-to article, procedural document, specification. Examples: an article on 'How to install Linux', a troubleshooting guide for a software error, a specification document for a new API.

candidates.label: SuspendAction
candidates.comment: The act of momentarily pausing a device, application, or process. Also called pausing, halting, putting on hold, temporarily stopping. Examples: pausing music playback, suspending a computer process, pausing a timer.

candidates.label: Error
candidates.comment: An Error is an InstantaneousEvent representing a problem or failure that occurred. Also called fault, malfunction, issue. Examples: A 404 Not Found error, a database connection error, a system crash, a data validation error.

candidates.label: BioChemEntity
candidates.comment: A fundamental Thing representing any biological, chemical, or biochemical substance or entity. Also called biochemical, chemical compound, biological entity, molecule. Examples: "A protein molecule", "A specific gene sequence", "A synthetic chemical compound", "DNA".

candidates.label: LoseAction
candidates.comment: The act of being defeated in a competitive activity or contest. Also called suffer defeat, be beaten, fail to win. Examples: losing a game, being defeated in an election, failing a competition. Distinct from AchieveAction, which is a broader category for actions that result in an outcome.

candidates.label: TypeAndQuantityNode
candidates.comment: A structured value indicating the quantity, unit of measurement, and business function of goods within a bundle offer. Also called quantity specification, offer item details, bundle component. Examples: "3 kg of apples for sale", "2 units of product X as a bonus", "1 liter of milk in a grocery bundle".

candidates.label: WarrantyPromise
candidates.comment: A structured value representing the duration and scope of free services provided for a product's defects or malfunctions. Also called product warranty, guarantee, service promise. Examples: a 1-year manufacturer's warranty, a 90-day repair guarantee, a lifetime parts warranty.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

candidates.label: GovernmentOffice
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOffice is a local business representing a specific governmental agency or department. Also called public agency office, state department branch, municipal service center. Examples: IRS office, DMV office, local planning department, social security office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is the physical structure that may contain multiple offices.

candidates.label: GovernmentService
candidates.comment: A GovernmentService is an intangible service provided by a government organization to the public. Also called public service, state-provided service, municipal offering. Examples: food stamps program, veterans benefits, public education, waste collection.

candidates.label: GovernmentBenefitsType
candidates.comment: GovernmentBenefitsType is an enumeration of various government benefits, particularly those related to supporting situations like COVID-19. candidates.label: GovernmentPermit
candidates.comment: A GovernmentPermit is a formal authorization issued by a government agency. Also called public license, state approval, official authorization. Examples: building permit, driver's license, business operating license, fishing permit.

types.embedding_query_text: ActionCategory Examples: unauthorized actions.

chosen_type.definition: A classification or type of action.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly represents an 'ActionCategory'. It is an intangible classification of actions.

candidates.label: AuthenticateAction
candidates.comment: An AuthenticateAction is a ControlAction representing the act of verifying one's identity to gain access to a device or application. Also called log in, sign in, verify identity, authorize access. Examples: logging into a website, unlocking a phone with a password, using a fingerprint scanner to access an app, authenticating with a two-factor code.

candidates.label: ActionAccessSpecification
candidates.comment: An ActionAccessSpecification is an Intangible item detailing the requirements that must be met to perform a specific Action. Also called access requirements, action prerequisites, permission rules. Examples: "Requires login," "Subscription needed," "Age 18+," "Admin privileges."

candidates.label: AuthorizeAction
candidates.comment: An AuthorizeAction is an AllocateAction representing the act of granting permission or approval for an object or action. Also called grant permission, approve, sanction, permit, allow. Examples: authorizing a payment, granting access to a file, approving a request, permitting a user to perform an action. Distinct from AuthenticateAction, which is about verifying identity, whereas AuthorizeAction is about granting permissions after identity is verified.

candidates.label: DeactivateAction
candidates.comment: An action that involves stopping or turning off a device, application, or process. Also called Turn off, disable, shut down, stop. Examples: Turning off a light, deactivating an alarm, stopping a timer, disabling a software feature. Distinct from ActivateAction, which is the act of starting or enabling something.

candidates.label: LoginAction
candidates.comment: The action of gaining access to a device or application by providing credentials. Also called sign in, log on, user authentication. Examples: logging into a website, signing into a mobile app, logging onto a computer. Distinct from ControlAction, which is a broader category for actions that control something.
